clue.text: Left workplace with speech on company teamwork

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the earlier pieces come after the company

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory, is a scientist's workplace
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Someone quits the office and gives a speech about how the firm works together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the company's CO at the front, ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Working together jointly with others is cooperation, a synonym of teamwork.

clue.text: Abundant signs of debt covered by policeman

indicators.note: in a down entry, being covered by something means lying beneath it, so the debt signs follow the policeman

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
IOUs are written promises to repay, so plural signs of debt

explanation.surface: A police officer is weighed down by a great pile of unpaid notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful supplies are described as copious, a straight synonym.

clue.text: European in bustling Darlington withdrawing to old city

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another is placed inside it, here the European letter inside the scrambled town
bustling suggests busy jostling movement, so the letters are stirred into a new order
withdrawing means pulling out, so the word to is taken out of the town's name

explanation.surface: A visitor from Europe in a busy northern English town retreats to an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' removes T and O from DARLINGTON, leaving DARLINGN; 'bustling' scrambles that to LNINGRAD, and E goes in. Darlington is a town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: St Petersburg bore the Soviet-era name from 1924 to 1991, so it is a former city name.

clue.text: Tolerate a US president dispatching the last

indicators.note: dispatching means getting rid of, so the final letter of the president's name is dropped

parts.note: Joe Biden was the 46th US president

explanation.surface: Put up with an American leader who has just got rid of his predecessor.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with or stand something is to bear it, a synonym.

clue.text: Old swimmer borne by swimming stroke in cool manner

indicators.note: being borne by something means being carried inside it, so the swimmer goes within the stroke

parts.note: fly is short for butterfly, the swimming stroke
a fish is a creature that swims

explanation.surface: An aged fish carried along by a butterfly swimmer, described in an aloof way.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmer goes between F and LY of the stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving distantly or standoffishly is acting coolly, the adverb's sense.

clue.text: Mark of character that directs stress?

definitions.text: Mark of character that directs stress?

parts.words: Mark of character that directs stress?
parts.note: a character here is a written letter, and the mark above it tells the reader where to put emphasis in speaking

explanation.surface: A sign of personality that tells people how to handle pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like personality and 'stress' like strain, but they are a letter and spoken emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks like the acute sign over a letter show pronunciation and emphasis, so this diacritic fits.

clue.text: Independent politician on tour making advances

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
roving means wandering about, as when on tour

explanation.surface: A non-party politician travels about the country and wins support.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting better or progressing means making headway, so advancing fits.

clue.text: Unfeasible going north or south

indicators.note: in a down entry north is upwards and south downwards, so the letters read the same either way up the grid

parts.note: an idiom for something that cannot be allowed or done, and its letters read the same both ways

explanation.surface: It cannot be done whichever direction you travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, so reading it up or down the grid gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something unacceptable or impossible to allow, close to unworkable.

clue.text: Drunk beginning to bet on game

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken here from bet

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A tipsy gambler starts putting money on a numbers game.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for very intoxicated, a synonym of drunk.

clue.text: Priest is quiet about squabble

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
on can mean concerning or about, as in a talk on art
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A clergyman keeps his voice down about a minor row.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope or any bishop is a high priest, the Latin pontifex.

clue.text: Outdo one regularly at fault — excellent

parts.note: to cap something is to top or better it
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of at fault is taken

explanation.surface: Someone at fault manages to outdo the others and comes out splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'at fault', giving TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned British exclamation meaning first-rate or splendid.

clue.text: Measure something cricket ball does getting bowled out

indicators.note: out means removed, and bowled is B in cricket scoring, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a cricket ball bounces off the pitch before reaching the batsman

explanation.surface: A cricket ball's behaviour is gauged when the batsman is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring B stands for bowled, one way a batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound, so a measure.

clue.text: Dishevelled on nun, best headwear

indicators.note: dishevelled means messed up and untidy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A scruffy nun turns up in her finest hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed hat shading the face and neck is an item worn on the head.

clue.text: Daughter admitted to mixed results making puddings

indicators.note: being admitted to a place means let inside it, so the daughter goes in the jumble
mixed means jumbled together, so the letters of results are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl let into a set of mixed exam grades results in desserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered pastry desserts with apple filling, so British puddings.

clue.text: Break down artistic style with male model

parts.note: Deco, as in Art Deco, is a decorative style of the 1920s and 30s
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: An Art Deco look with a man posing for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic matter that rots is said to break down or decay.

clue.text: This writer's working wearing knockout attire

indicators.note: something wearing a garment has it around it, so the knockout letters enclose the rest

parts.note: the writer speaking of themselves says I am, contracted to I'm
on means working or operating, as in switched on

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be busy while dressed in something stunning.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose Japanese robe tied with a sash, a kind of clothing.

clue.text: So wire the explosive in a different way

indicators.note: something explosive blows apart, so these letters are blasted into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to connect up a bomb differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by another method or differently, the adverb's sense.

clue.text: Choose strange alloy

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An odd selection made from metals.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural blend of gold and silver used for ancient coins, so an alloy.

clue.text: Departs English Channel for dock

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
a duct is a channel or tube for fluid

explanation.surface: A ferry leaves the English Channel heading for port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' is the verb meaning to take money off, as in docking wages, not a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Docking pay means subtracting from it, so the two verbs mean take away.

clue.text: Dislike cuddling partner keeping TV turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom, so the whole is written backwards
keeping means holding within, so the bear surrounds the television

parts.note: Ted, short for teddy bear, is a soft toy to cuddle
a TV set is a television

explanation.surface: Someone hates a partner who snuggles up with the television blaring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuddling partner' is the teddy bear, not a lover; 'keeping' and 'turned up' build the word from the bottom of the grid upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or hate intensely is a strong form of dislike.

clue.text: Fellow falls behind in important vessel

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind
in and hip both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A man trails behind but still gets on board the main ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading ship of a fleet carries the admiral, so the most important vessel.

clue.text: Mineral — it's found in piles of combustible material

indicators.note: being found in something means located inside it, so it goes within the piles

parts.note: pyres are heaps of wood for burning a body
it, with the 's read as is linking to the containment

explanation.surface: A mineral turns up among heaps of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron sulphide, known as fool's gold, is a common crystalline mineral.

clue.text: Crooks gutted stores either side of river

indicators.note: placed on either side means flanking, so the outer letters wrap round the river
a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the Taff is a river in South Wales flowing through Cardiff

explanation.surface: Criminals strip a shop's contents, operating on both banks of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd's crook is a long hooked stick, a type of walking stick.

clue.text: A jerk on vehicle carrying you, reportedly painful

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another follows it, so the jerk comes after the vehicle
carrying means holding within, so the vehicle surrounds the letter

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle on rails

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word you is replaced by the single letter sounding like it

parts.note: the letter U sounds like you
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: An idiot on a tram is giving a passenger a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like an idiot but is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deeply distressing or emotionally wounding is hurtful, close to painful.

clue.text: In area, going to avoid centre

indicators.note: avoiding the centre means skipping the middle letters of the word

parts.note: going means moving, as in on the go

explanation.surface: Travelling around a district while steering clear of the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid centre' drops VI, the middle two letters of MOVING.
explanation.definitionFit: Being amid or surrounded by others, as in one in a crowd, so a preposition of inclusion.

clue.text: Second bishop getting cut from hairdresser is balder

indicators.note: being cut from means removed, so that letter leaves the hairdresser

parts.note: a barber cuts men's hair
B is bishop in chess notation, and the second of the two Bs is the one dropped

explanation.surface: A clergyman's trim at the barber leaves him with less hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Having less covering or hair means more exposed, a comparative synonym.

clue.text: Account penned by good Parisian writer

indicators.note: being penned by something means enclosed by it, as in a pen, so the account goes inside

parts.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A report written by a fine French author.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon wrote the essays and The Advancement of Learning, so a famous English writer.

clue.text: Close to worthless house, posh person rushed away

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of worthless is taken

parts.note: a toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A snob near a run-down house hurries off.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving very quickly is shooting away, an idiom for rushing off.

clue.text: Getting set-piece, right back crosses

indicators.note: back means turned around, so the picked letters are read in reverse
letters crossed by the phrase lie across its word breaks, so they are taken from inside it

explanation.surface: A football match report: a free kick, and the right back sends over crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards across 'set-piece, right'. 'Getting' is the noun, the act of receiving.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipt is formal usage for the act of receiving, as in on receipt of goods.

clue.text: Mechanics say green smoke is unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Engine workers remark that green exhaust smoke is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for car mechanics, who are usually covered in oil.
